universal_lens: Multi-task learning unifies fine-grained spatial prediction through shared representations, enabling consistent distributional forecasts across heterogeneous sport analytics. Rugby-Bot integrates multi-task spatial learning via fine-grained tackle-level data to infer game state across play, set, and game resolutions using probabilistic forecasting.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference maps multi-task outputs to posterior predictive distributions, supporting conformal uncertainty quantification for sport performance metrics. GSI employs Bayesian inference to map contextual spatial insights into posterior distributions over expected meters, try probabilities, and scorelines, enabling real-time risk assessment.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning encodes state transitions via fine-grained spatial features; GSE models dynamic play evolution using wide-and-deep embeddings and temporal consistency. GSE utilizes conformal predictive systems to model state transitions between tackles, incorporating momentum, field position, and score differential into dynamic decision trees.

primitives.name: Negative Log-Likelihood Loss

primitives.assumptions: The primary assumption is that the model provides a valid probability distribution over the output space. The NLL loss encourages the model to assign high probability to the true observed outcomes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When the model's predicted distribution is highly confident but wrong (i.e., overconfident), the NLL loss will be very large.
